feature: An icon exported as a picture can leave its canvas out
summary: An icon drawn on a blank canvas now exports as a PNG with nothing behind the shapes, so it can be dropped on a coloured page or a dark theme without a white box round it. The Export sheet asks with the same Include the background checkbox SVG has, in the same place, and never asks for a format that cannot hold transparency.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to switch on.

try.do: File ▸ New Canvas, take the default size.
Press P for the Pen and draw a closed shape a few clicks across.
Read the row under the pixel size: Include the background, unticked, with a swatch of the canvas colour.
Press Export… and save the PNG, then open it over something dark (a dark Finder Quick Look, a dark web page).
Press ⌘E again, tick Include the background, and save a second PNG: that one carries the white.
Press ⌘E and pick JPEG: the row is gone, because a JPEG cannot hold see-through pixels.
Open a screenshot instead of a blank canvas and press ⌘E: no row at all, and the picture exports with its background as it always did.

evaluate: Is unticked the right default for PNG, given a picture drawn on a blank canvas now goes out see-through unless you say otherwise?
Does the row read clearly enough under the pixel size, or does it want to sit somewhere else on the sheet?
Is the swatch at the far right of the row doing its job, or is it too far from the words it belongs to?
Was it obvious the exported PNG would be see-through before you opened it, or did you have to check?
Should copying the picture (⇧⌘C) do the same thing, or is a paste always expected to carry the canvas?
rough: The two pictures here are real screen captures, but the Mac reported its screen locked while the walk ran, so the colours in them are dimmed: the white canvas reads grey and the shape reads dull red. What the pictures are being shown for, the row and its words, is unaffected.
PNG shows no file size on the sheet, so you cannot see the file get smaller when the canvas goes. Only the lossy formats weigh themselves.
Copying the picture with ⇧⌘C still carries the white canvas: the change is on the Export path only. Filed as its own task.
The swatch sits hard right of the sheet, a long way from the checkbox it explains. That is inherited from the SVG row rather than new here, so it was left alone.
